lessons.title: Introduction and Why It Matters
lessons.body: When you finish fabricating a gate, window grille, or balustrade in the workshop, it must be installed correctly on site. Poor installation can ruin your work: a gate that doesn't swing, a grille that rattles, or a railing that wobbles. In Africa, sites vary widelyâfrom sandy coastal plots to rocky hillside compounds. You must adapt to mud, dust, uneven ground, and sometimes no electricity. A proper installation ensures security, safety, and customer satisfaction. It also protects your reputation. If a gate falls off its hinges after a month, you lose future jobs. This module teaches you how to plan, prepare, and execute a professional installation. You will learn to measure accurately, choose the right fixings, handle tools safely, and avoid common mistakes. We focus on practical methods using locally available materials like rawl bolts, cement, and welding machines. Whether you are installing a simple window grille in a Nairobi apartment or a large driveway gate in Lagos, the principles are the same. By the end, you will be able to install ornamental ironwork that is strong, level, and beautiful. Remember: a good installation is invisibleâthe customer only sees the finished product working perfectly. That is your goal.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials
lessons.body: To install ornamental ironwork on site, you need a core set of tools and materials. Start with a heavy-duty hammer drill (e.g., Bosch GBH 2-26) and masonry bits sized for your fixingsâtypically 8mm, 10mm, and 12mm. For gates, you need a spirit level (600mm or 1200mm), a measuring tape (5m), a plumb bob or laser level, and a chalk line. A welding machine (portable inverter like ESAB or Lincoln) with electrodes (2.5mm or 3.2mm) is essential for on-site adjustments. You will also need an angle grinder with cutting and grinding discs, a set of spanners, a socket set, and a rubber mallet. For fixings, use galvanised rawl bolts (M8 or M10) for concrete, or chemical anchors (e.g., Hilti HIT) for cracked or hollow blocks. In many African markets, you can buy these at hardware shops in industrial areas. For gates, heavy-duty hinges (weld-on or bolt-on) and gate wheels (if sliding) are needed. For balustrades, base plates and anchor bolts. Bring cement (Portland 32.5 or 42.5) for grouting, plus sand and water if you need to patch. Safety gear: gloves, safety glasses, ear defenders, dust mask, and steel-toe boots. A generator may be necessary if site power is unreliable. Always carry a first-aid kit. Organise your tools in a sturdy bag or bucket so you don't lose small items in the mud. Before leaving the workshop, check that you have everythingâreturning for a missing 10mm bit wastes half a day.

lessons.title: Step by Step Method
lessons.body: Follow these steps for a typical installation of a metal gate or window grille. First, measure the opening precisely. Use a tape and record width at top, middle, and bottom; height at left, right, and centre. The smallest dimension is your critical size. Allow 5-10mm clearance for gates and 2-3mm for grilles. Second, prepare the surface. Remove loose concrete, dust, and paint. For masonry, drill holes with a hammer drill at the marked positions. Hold the drill perpendicular; go 10mm deeper than the bolt length. Blow out dust with a pump or compressed air. Third, position the ironwork. For a gate, lift it into the opening using two people or a tripod. Check level and plumb with a spirit level. Use wooden wedges to hold it temporarily. Fourth, fix the anchors. For rawl bolts, insert them and tighten with a spanner until the sleeve expands. For chemical anchors, inject resin, insert the stud, and let it cure for the time specified (usually 30-60 minutes). Fifth, weld or bolt hinges and locks. Tack weld first, check movement, then complete the weld. For grilles, plug weld to embedded plates or use bolts. Sixth, grout around base plates with cement mortar (1 part cement to 3 parts sand). Seventh, test operation. Open and close the gate several times; adjust hinges or add washers if needed. Finally, clean up: remove metal shavings, touch up paint, and show the customer how to use the lock. On a recent site in Accra, a team installed a 3m sliding gate in 4 hours using this method. Always work in pairs for heavy items.

lessons.title: Common Mistakes and Fixes
lessons.body: Even experienced installers make mistakes. Here are common ones and how to fix them. Mistake 1: Not checking level. A gate that leans will swing open or closed by itself. Fix: Use a spirit level on both the gate frame and the posts. If already installed, loosen anchors, re-level with shims, and re-tighten. Mistake 2: Insufficient anchors. Using only two bolts for a heavy gate leads to wobbling. Fix: Use at least four anchors per post, spaced evenly. For large gates, add a centre anchor. Mistake 3: Wrong drill bit size. A hole too large makes the bolt loose; too small prevents insertion. Fix: Match bit to bolt diameterâe.g., 10mm bolt needs 10mm bit for rawl, but 12mm for chemical anchors. Always test on a scrap piece. Mistake 4: Ignoring expansion. Metal expands in heat. In hot African climates, leave a 5mm gap between gate and post. Fix: If gate jams in afternoon, grind a small amount off the latch or hinge. Mistake 5: Poor welding on site. Wind can blow away shielding gas or cause porosity. Fix: Use stick electrodes (e.g., E6013) and shield the weld area with a piece of metal. Mistake 6: Not protecting finishes. Welding spatter damages paint. Fix: Cover nearby surfaces with fire blanket or wet cloth. Mistake 7: Rushing the cure. Chemical anchors need full cure time. Fix: Wait at least 30 minutes before loading. If a mistake happens, don't hide itâtell the customer and fix it immediately. A small repair now saves a big problem later.

lessons.title: Safety and Best Practice
lessons.body: Safety on site is non-negotiable. Before you start, conduct a risk assessment: look for overhead power lines, uneven ground, and bystanders. Always wear personal protective equipment (PPE): safety glasses, gloves, ear defenders, dust mask, and steel-toe boots. When using a hammer drill, keep both hands on the tool and be ready for kickback. For welding, wear a welding helmet with the correct shade (e.g., shade 10 for stick welding), leather apron, and fire-resistant gloves. Never weld near flammable materialsâin Africa, dry grass or petrol cans are common hazards. Keep a fire extinguisher (dry powder) nearby. When lifting heavy gates, use proper lifting techniques: bend your knees, keep your back straight, and get help. Use a tripod or chain hoist for gates over 50kg. Ensure electrical tools are connected to a residual current device (RCD) or earth leakage breaker. If using a generator, ground it properly. Best practice includes: plan your work, keep the site tidy, and communicate with the customer. Protect finished surfaces with cardboard or tape during installation. After work, clean up all metal shavingsâthey can cause cuts or rust stains. Dispose of waste responsibly. In many African communities, it's customary to greet the client and explain what you're doing. This builds trust and reduces interruptions. Finally, never work alone on high-risk tasks; have a helper. If you feel unwell or tired, stop. A safe installer is a productive installer.

lessons.title: Practical Exercise
lessons.body: Now it's time to practice. This exercise simulates a real installation. You will install a small window grille (900mm x 900mm) into a concrete block wall. You need: a grille with four pre-drilled 10mm holes in its frame, four M10 rawl bolts, a hammer drill with 10mm bit, a spirit level, a tape measure, a spanner, and safety gear. Step 1: Measure the window opening. Mark the centre of each hole on the wall using the grille as a template. Step 2: Drill four holes 60mm deep. Clean dust. Step 3: With a partner, lift the grille into place. Insert rawl bolts and tighten by hand. Step 4: Check level and plumb. Adjust by tapping with a rubber mallet. Step 5: Tighten bolts fully with a spanner. Step 6: Test the grilleâit should not move when pushed. Step 7: Grout around the frame with cement mortar if there are gaps. Step 8: Clean up and inspect for any damage. For advanced practice, install a small gate (1.2m wide) with hinges. Record your time and any problems. Discuss with your trainer: What went well? What would you change? In a real African context, you might face dusty conditions or uneven wallsâpractice shimming and using chemical anchors. Repeat this exercise until you can complete it in under 30 minutes with perfect level. This skill will make you employable.

quiz.q: What is the main reason proper installation matters for ornamental ironwork?
options: A) It makes the work look shiny
B) It ensures security, safety, and customer satisfaction
C) It reduces the cost of materials
D) It allows you to use less welding
quiz.explanation: Proper installation ensures the ironwork functions correctly, providing security and safety, which leads to customer satisfaction.

quiz.q: Which tool is essential for drilling holes in concrete walls during installation?
quiz.explanation: A hammer drill is specifically designed for drilling into masonry and concrete.

quiz.q: What is the recommended clearance for a gate installation?
quiz.explanation: A 5-10mm clearance allows for expansion and smooth operation without jamming.

quiz.q: What should you do if a gate leans after installation?
options: A) Ignore it, it will settle
C) Loosen anchors, re-level with shims, and re-tighten
D) Cut the gate to fit
quiz.explanation: Re-leveling with shims corrects the lean without damaging the gate or frame.

quiz.q: Which PPE is necessary when welding on site?
options: B) Welding helmet with correct shade
quiz.explanation: A welding helmet protects eyes and face from harmful UV radiation and sparks.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when drilling holes for rawl bolts?
options: A) Using a drill bit that is too small
C) Not cleaning dust from holes
quiz.explanation: All these mistakes can weaken the fixing; correct bit size, depth, and cleaning are crucial.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of grouting around base plates?
options: A) To make it look pretty
B) To provide a solid, weatherproof base
quiz.explanation: Grout fills gaps and protects against moisture, ensuring a stable installation.

quiz.q: How many anchors are recommended for a heavy gate post?
quiz.explanation: At least four anchors distribute load and prevent wobbling.

quiz.q: What should you do before lifting a heavy gate?
options: B) Use a tripod or get help
quiz.explanation: Using a tripod or helper prevents injury and damage to the gate.

quiz.q: Which of these is a best practice for site safety?
options: A) Work alone on high-risk tasks
B) Keep site tidy and communicate with customer
D) Skip PPE to save time
quiz.explanation: A tidy site and clear communication reduce accidents and build trust.

quiz.q: What is the first step in the step-by-step installation method?
quiz.explanation: Accurate measurement ensures the ironwork fits correctly from the start.

quiz.q: Why should you blow out dust from drilled holes?
options: A) To make the hole look clean
B) To ensure the anchor bonds properly
C) To cool the drill bit
quiz.explanation: Dust prevents the anchor from gripping, so cleaning is essential for strength.

quiz.q: What is a sign of poor welding on site?
options: B) Porosity or holes in weld
quiz.explanation: Porosity indicates trapped gas, weakening the weld, often due to wind or moisture.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before loading a chemical anchor?
quiz.explanation: Chemical anchors require full cure time (typically 30-60 minutes) to reach strength.

quiz.q: What is the correct cement-to-sand ratio for grouting?
quiz.explanation: A 1:3 mix provides good strength and workability for grouting.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common mistake with expansion gaps?
quiz.explanation: No gap can cause jamming in hot weather due to metal expansion.

quiz.q: What should you do if you make a mistake during installation?
options: C) Tell the customer and fix it immediately
quiz.explanation: Honesty and immediate correction maintain trust and quality.

quiz.q: Why is it important to use an RCD with electrical tools?
options: B) It protects against electric shock
quiz.explanation: An RCD (earth leakage breaker) cuts power if a fault occurs, preventing electrocution.

quiz.q: What is the recommended clearance for a window grille?
quiz.explanation: A small 2-3mm clearance allows for fitting without rattling.

quiz.q: In the practical exercise, what size rawl bolts are used?
quiz.explanation: The exercise specifies M10 rawl bolts for the grille.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do when arriving on site?
quiz.explanation: A risk assessment identifies hazards before work begins, ensuring safety.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good practice when lifting heavy items?
options: B) Keep load close to body
quiz.explanation: Keeping the load close reduces strain on the back.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a plumb bob or laser level?
quiz.explanation: A plumb bob checks if a post or gate is perfectly vertical.

quiz.q: Why should you protect finished surfaces during installation?
options: B) To prevent weld spatter and scratches
quiz.explanation: Protection prevents damage that would require costly rework.

quiz.q: What is a common fix for a gate that jams in hot weather?
options: B) Grind a small amount off the latch or hinge
quiz.explanation: Grinding creates extra clearance to accommodate expansion.

quiz.q: Which anchor type is best for cracked concrete?
quiz.explanation: Chemical anchors bond to the concrete, providing strength even in cracked material.

quiz.q: What should you do after completing installation?
options: B) Clean up and test operation
quiz.explanation: Testing and cleaning ensure the product works and the site is safe.

quiz.q: Why is it important to have a first-aid kit on site?
options: A) To treat minor cuts and burns
quiz.explanation: A first-aid kit allows immediate treatment of common injuries like cuts and burns.

quiz.q: What is the recommended drill depth for a 60mm long rawl bolt?
quiz.explanation: Drill 10mm deeper than the bolt length to allow for dust and full insertion.

quiz.q: In the practical exercise, what is the target completion time?
quiz.explanation: The exercise aims for completion in under 30 minutes with perfect level.
